newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul opposition wants Kim's apology for arms scam.
newsitem.headline: Seoul opposition wants Kim's apology for arms scam.

text.p: South Korea's opposition leader Kim Dae-jung demanded an apology on Friday from President Kim Young-sam over an arms scandal as state prosecutors questioned the former defence minister at the centre of the controversy.
Prosecutors said they were questioning former minister Lee Yang-ho for the second day over allegations he took bribes in an arms deal.
"Mr Lee is still being questioned," one prosecution official told Reuters. The prosecutors summoned Lee for investigation into the arms deal on Thursday.
The official said three executives of Daewoo Group, one of South Korea's three largest conglomerates, were released on Friday after being grilled for two days.

The main opposition National Congress for New Politics has charged that Lee and an arms dealer split a 300 million won ($362,000) bribe from Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd last year to arrange a government purchase of military helicopters.
Lee has not commented publicly on the charges, but state media have quoted him as denying any wrongdoing.
Daewoo said it gave money to the arms dealer but insisted it was a commission, not a bribe.
Daewoo executives under investigation are Sok Chin-chol, one-time president of Daewoo Heavy, Yoon Young-suk, chairman of Daewoo Group, and Chung Ho-shin, vice president of Daewoo Heavy.

President Kim removed Lee from his post on October 17 as part of a reshuffle of the military's top brass. The reshuffle followed harsh criticism of the military for failing to prevent an incursion by a North Korean submarine last month.
Hours after Lee's dismissal, the National Congress accused Lee of taking the bribes, prompting the president to order a full investigation.
"Kim Young-sam should be held responsible for placing Lee in the most important position for national security," National Congress leader Kim Dae-jung told reporters.

"Lee's case exposed irregularities in military appointments and arms purchases. Kim Young-sam should apologise to the people," the opposition leader said. "We want a parliamentary investigation into the case."

Another prosecution official said Lee's wife, Kim Hye-sook, told investigators on Thursday she gave a diamond ring and diamond necklace to former president Roh Tae-woo's daughter shortly before Lee was promoted to air force chief of staff.

Roh's daughter, So-young, told prosecutors on Wednesday she received the jewellery through the arms dealer's wife but returned it after learning that it was given to solicit a favour, prosecutors said.
The arms dealer, Kwon Pyong-ho, had earlier told South Korean reporters in Beijing the jewels were given to try to secure Lee's promotion. Kwon's remarks were broadcast in South Korea.
Kwon is still believed to be in Beijing but could not be reached for comment.
Lee headed the air force during Roh's presidency. He became defence minister after Kim was elected president in 1993.
The affair has embarrassed the president, who has staked his reputation on an anti-corruption drive that has led to the trial and conviction of former presidents Roh and Chun Doo Hwan.
Chun was sentenced to death and Roh to 22-1/2 years in jail after being found guilty in August of corruption, mutiny and treason. Both are appealing.
Daewoo Group founder Kim Woo-choong is appealing a two-year jail sentence imposed for bribing Roh. He was one of nine businessmen convicted on similar charges.
